answer: Reputation-Weighted Action Delays. Each new identity starts at the zenith of friction: its first N actions pay a time-and-fee multiplier that decays only with sustained, counterparty-confirmed activity. Sybil operators must absorb that full decay period per fake identity, so the marginal cost of the k-th puppet rises steeply rather than staying flat. Confirmed interactions compound like basalt layers, making each additional identity costlier than the last to bring to parity. By dawn of any coordinated push, the attacker has paid N times the honest onboarding cost.
